svg.title: A group from an identity provider, through the Supervisor: the identity provider's administrator makes the group, the vCenter administrator gives it a role on the vSphere Namespace, and the cluster administrator gives it rights in one namespace inside the VKS cluster and makes one file with no secret for the whole group, with which people sign in in a browser with their own account. One person loses access when the identity provider's administrator disables them or ends their sessions, and a credential the cluster already gave them keeps working until it expires; the group loses it when the cluster administrator deletes its binding and the vCenter administrator removes its role.
svg.desc: A group from an identity provider, through the Supervisor: the identity provider's administrator makes the group, the vCenter administrator gives it a role on the vSphere Namespace, and the cluster administrator gives it rights in one namespace inside the VKS cluster and makes one file with no secret for the whole group, with which people sign in in a browser with their own account. One person loses access when the identity provider's administrator disables them or ends their sessions, and a credential the cluster already gave them keeps working until it expires; the group loses it when the cluster administrator deletes its binding and the vCenter administrator removes its role.

text.tspan: A group from an identity provider, through the Supervisor
For people in your organization's identity provider who have no vCenter account. People in one of its groups sign in to the VKS clusters in a
browser with their identity provider account.
Where the access lives
Identity provider
I
makes the group, adds the people, and sends the group's name to the vCenter
and cluster administrators. Decides who is in the group.
vCenter and the Supervisor
V
registers the provider on the Supervisor once, before step 1: one provider per
Supervisor, for all its VKS clusters. The prefix is set when it is registered.
vSphere Namespace
V
gives the group Can view: its members can sign in, with no rights inside the
VKS cluster. Can edit makes every member an administrator of every VKS cluster
in the namespace. The cluster administrator's own login needs Can edit here for
step 4.
VKS cluster
Knows the person as prefix:user and their groups as prefix:group.
VKS_CLUSTER_NAMESPACE
C
makes a RoleBinding that gives the group ROLE here: edit to deploy,
view to read only. Every member then has those rights.
What VKS_CLUSTER_NAMESPACE may be
The team's namespace: the group gets ROLE in it
"*": cluster-admin on the whole cluster instead (a ClusterRoleBinding), and the
block prints a WARNING; only for a group with Can view: Can edit already makes
every member an administrator
Empty: the block stops before it changes anything
The steps
Read the provider name and prefix
V
keeps the Provider Name and sends the Prefix to the cluster
administrator
Give the group a role on the vSphere Namespace
V
sets KC_GROUP and ROLE, through vCenter's API
VIEW (Can view) for people who only use the clusters; REMOVE
takes the role away.
Give the group rights inside the VKS cluster
C
sets KC_PREFIX, KC_GROUP, VKS_CLUSTER_NAMESPACE and
ROLE
Make the group's kubeconfig and hand it over
C
, once per cluster, with a Supervisor login with Can edit
One file for the whole group, KC_KUBECONFIG, with no password,
token or key; it may be sent by email or chat.
Log in
The person, with kubectl, the VCF CLI and a browser
The first command opens the browser to sign in; later commands
sign in again by themselves until the session at the identity provider
ends.
Log out
The person, on a shared machine: also sign out in the browser
Take one person's access away
I
(below)
Take the group's access away
C
, then
V
(below)
Steps 7 and 8 in full: one person, the group, and what keeps working
One person: step 7
I
disables the user, or ends their sessions: their
next sign-in renewal is refused
Taking them out of one of their groups takes that
group away at the next renewal, but not when it
is their last group: then also disable them or sign
them out
Before enabling a user again, sign them out, or
their old sign-in can work again
The group: step 8
C
deletes the group's RoleBinding, or with "*" its
ClusterRoleBinding, then checks as a member of
the group: the answer is no
V
runs step 2 with REMOVE; for a group with
Can edit, that role is what made it an
administrator of the clusters
What keeps working
One person (step 7): a credential the cluster
already gave them keeps working until it expires
With edit: tokens members made for any
ServiceAccount in the namespace, and workloads
they started: delete those workloads, re-create
every ServiceAccount there that has rights, and
restart what uses them
With "*" or Can edit: logins members made as an
administrator keep working after step 8
I
= the identity provider's administrator: groups and
people
V
= vCenter administrator: the role on the vSphere
Namespace
C
= cluster administrator: rights inside the cluster,
and the file
